userStories.title: Registrar tokens-por-ciclo no event log no cycle-close
userStories.description: As the cam orchestrator loop, I need the cycle-close step to persist a durable per-cycle token record (orchestrator session spend + the cycle's worker tokens) so that future per-issue token analysis (CAM-136) has the raw data, before the orchestrator context is reset by the per-cycle handoff.
acceptanceCriteria: A new exported function (e.g. recordCycleTokens) in src/commands/journal.ts emits one durable WorkerEvent of kind 'cycle-tokens' to .claude/cam-worker-events.jsonl whose detail carries {cycleId, issueNumber, orchTokens, workerTokens, total, recordedAt}. [oracle: grep -q "cycle-tokens" src/commands/journal.ts]

orchTokens is the CUMULATIVE orchestrator session spend (input + cacheCreation + cacheRead) computed by parseTranscriptUsage over the transcript resolved by orchestratorTranscriptPath; the simple model is used (cumulative session, NOT a baseline-delta), per the operator decision. [oracle: grep -q "parseTranscriptUsage\|orchestratorTranscriptPath" src/commands/journal.ts]

workerTokens is the sum of the cycle's worker 'tokens' events read back from the event log (the per-cycle slice: worker 'tokens' events appended after the previous 'cycle-tokens' marker); a worker total token equals inputTokens + outputTokens + cacheReadTokens + cacheCreationTokens (the exact TokensEventDetail fields in src/supervisor/events.ts). [oracle: bun test]
total === orchTokens + workerTokens in the emitted record. [oracle: bun test]
All filesystem and transcript reads plus the event logger are injectable so a unit test asserts the emitted 'cycle-tokens' detail shape without touching real ~/.claude or git. [oracle: bun test]
When the orchestrator transcript is absent/unreadable, orchTokens records 0 (not an error) and the 'cycle-tokens' event is still emitted. [oracle: bun test]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Full gate spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: src/commands/journal.ts (new recordCycleTokens helper + new 'cycle-tokens' WorkerEventKind in src/supervisor/events.ts WorkerEventKind union + a CycleTokensEventDetail interface). Reuse parseTranscriptUsage + orchestratorTranscriptPath from src/transcript/usage.ts (do NOT reinvent token counting). Reuse makeFileEventLogger / WorkerEvent / TokensEventDetail from src/supervisor/events.ts. TokensEventDetail field names are EXACT: inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheCreationTokens (src/supervisor/events.ts:105-115); a worker's per-cycle total = inputTokens + outputTokens + cacheReadTokens + cacheCreationTokens. Do NOT invent abbreviated field names. Per the grilled spec (spec.scope, gotcha #1): orch-budget metric is CUMULATIVE traffic (~5.58M real), so do NOT use a threshold; just record the cumulative session spend as ~tokens-of-cycle (transcript zeros each cycle once CAM-131 lands, per the operator's baseline decision). Worker tokens come from the existing 'tokens' events (storyId+uuid keyed) emitted in src/supervisor/loop.ts:~582; the per-cycle slice is the worker 'tokens' events after the last 'cycle-tokens' event in the cumulative log. Event log path: .claude/cam-worker-events.jsonl (EVENT_LOG_PATH in src/commands/dashboard.ts:50; reader pattern at dashboard.ts:551 split('\n') + JSON.parse). domainTerms 'tokens-por-ciclo' lives in the issue spec, not in a CONTEXT.md (writer CAM-118 does not exist yet). DECISAO do operador: modelo SIMPLES, sem baseline-marker; analise de delta/media e CAM-136 separado.

userStories.title: Emitir sinal incondicional de handoff no journal append
userStories.description: As the cam orchestrator, I need cam journal append to print CAM_ORCH_HANDOFF_DUE=true strictly after the journal entry and the per-cycle token record are persisted, so that I receive a deterministic, threshold-free trigger to hand off at the cycle boundary (and only there).
acceptanceCriteria: After a successful appendJournalEntryOnMain AND after the US-001 cycle-tokens record is persisted, the cam journal append path emits the line CAM_ORCH_HANDOFF_DUE=true UNCONDITIONALLY (no token threshold gates it). [oracle: grep -q "CAM_ORCH_HANDOFF_DUE=true" index.ts src/commands/journal.ts]
The signal is emitted ONLY on a successful append (not when the result is !ok); on failure no CAM_ORCH_HANDOFF_DUE line is printed. [oracle: bun test]

The signal line is printed AFTER the CAM_JOURNAL_APPENDED=<cycleId> sha=<sha> line and AFTER the cycle-tokens event is written, guaranteeing durable memory is saved before the orchestrator resets. [oracle: bun test]

A unit test through dispatchJournal (injecting appendFn + writeStdout) asserts both the CAM_JOURNAL_APPENDED line and the CAM_ORCH_HANDOFF_DUE=true line are emitted in order on success, and that CAM_ORCH_HANDOFF_DUE is absent on a failed append. [oracle: bun test]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Full gate spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: index.ts dispatchJournal (~line 1051-1089; the CAM_JOURNAL_APPENDED writeStdout is at index.ts:1087) and/or src/commands/journal.ts. Sequence is load-bearing: journal entry persisted -> US-001 cycle-tokens event persisted -> THEN CAM_ORCH_HANDOFF_DUE=true. Wire the US-001 recordCycleTokens call into the same dispatch path before the signal. orch-budget/threshold STOPS gatilhando (per spec.scope + gotcha #1): src/commands/orch-budget.ts stays as a cost reporter only; do NOT remove it. Keep the existing dispatchJournal injectable-deps pattern (readStdin/appendFn/writeStdout) so the new behavior is testable without real I/O.

userStories.title: Resetar cap de respawn por progresso no wrapper do cam run
userStories.description: As the cam run orchestrator pane wrapper, I need to distinguish a cycle-close handoff (reason: cycle-close) from a no-progress handoff so that a per-cycle handoff resets the respawn counter and the session can drain the queue indefinitely, while the anti-loop backstop still tears down after N consecutive no-progress respawns.
acceptanceCriteria: buildOrchestratorPaneCommand (src/commands/run.ts) reads the handoff JSON's reason field via jq BEFORE consuming/renaming the handoff file (operator decision: jq, consistent with the CAM-91/96 hook). [oracle: grep -q "jq" src/commands/run.ts]
When reason == 'cycle-close', the wrapper resets the respawn counter to n=0; otherwise it increments n (no-progress backstop preserved). [oracle: bun test]

kill-session teardown fires only after N consecutive no-progress respawns reach the cap; DEFAULT_MAX_ORCH_RESPAWNS remains the no-progress ceiling. [oracle: grep -q "DEFAULT_MAX_ORCH_RESPAWNS" src/commands/run.ts]

The fresh-uuid mint (uuidgen | tr A-Z a-z), .cam-orch-session rewrite, handoff rename to .consumed.json, bypassPermissions, stateFile/readyMarker cleanup, and the kill-session shape are all preserved unchanged except for the reason-based counter logic. [oracle: bun test]

buildOrchestratorPaneCommand remains pure string assembly (no I/O); a unit test asserts the produced bash contains the jq reason read, the n=0 reset on cycle-close, and the n increment otherwise. [oracle: bun test]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Full gate spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: File: src/commands/run.ts buildOrchestratorPaneCommand (~line 205-239; cap logic at lines 213/216/226, DEFAULT_MAX_ORCH_RESPAWNS at line 163). The bomb being fixed: the current `n >= max(5)` NEVER resets, so per-cycle handoff kills the session at the 6th cycle (gotcha #2). The reason field is read from the handoff at opts.handoffMarker BEFORE the `mv ... .consumed.json` rename. Use jq to extract .reason (operator decision; jq already a dependency per the CAM-91/96 hook). The single-quote escaping helper `q()` must wrap any embedded path. Keep the macOS uuidgen lowercase gotcha (line 222 comment) intact. Reason value 'cycle-close' is written by the persona in US-004; schema field is `reason: string` in src/orchestrator/handoff.ts (OrchHandoffPayload). Test shape: assert on the assembled bash string (run.test.ts pattern), since the wrapper is pure string assembly.
